steps.description: MEM-CAP DERIVATION 2026-08-04 (follow-on to task memory-caps-must-scale-with-job-count / #1583, which MISSED this privileged-lane build node): pinned_jobs=8 literal via CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 prefix on BOTH build commands (was unset -> both cargo build and cargo test --no-run defaulted their build phase to nproc; that cc1plus fan-out is the OOM class the pin bounds; the job-pin is the actual fix). Cap KEPT at the existing generous 8.0GiB: a warm/incremental measurement read peak_bytes~1.64GiB @j8, but that reused build.workspace artifacts and UNDER-estimates a cold from-scratch privileged build, so the 8.0GiB headroom is retained rather than tightened on an unreliable warm figure. rss_baseline=5.0GiB (scheduling reservation). hermit@b384187e.
steps.cmd: CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo build -p hermit --features third-party-backends --bin hermit && CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 cargo test -p hermit-detcore --test tests_misc --no-run

steps.description: MOVED OUT OF e2e.metadata 2026-08-08, same reason as the portable lane: e2e.metadata is a DAG ROOT whose first action is a cargo build (it runs `cargo run -p hermit-manifest-plan` twice), so a light 60s test node was carrying a compile whose cost depends on cache state. WHY 19s HERE AND 180s IN portable, WHICH IS NOT AN INCONSISTENCY. The two lanes run on different hardware and the cold-compile cost differs by ~9x. portable runs on ubuntu-latest, where the cold compile measured 49.4-52.1s, so it needs a build-shaped 180s. THIS lane runs on the self-hosted [Linux, X64, hermit, pmu] boxes, where the same cold build measured 5.42s (cargo clean -p hermit-manifest-plan then rebuild, 2026-08-08) -- 19s is 3.5x that. The privileged lane is also structurally WARMER than portable: it has no Swatinem/rust-cache restore step to miss, because the self-hosted checkout persists target/ between runs, so the cold path here is the rare case rather than a coin flip. 19s IS THE MAXIMUM THIS LANE CAN AFFORD, and that is a hard arithmetic bound, not a preference: ci/test_harness.sh requires the 360s inner launcher to exceed the critical path plus 30s overhead, the baseline critical path is 310s, and this node sits on it, so timeout must satisfy 310 + t <= 329. Anyone adding a node to this lane's critical path must first raise that 360s launcher and the workflow job timeout above it.
